title: Replacing a date with an invalid date writes non-date bytes
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img, desktop route. USE EDGE; REPLACE WHEN WITH CTOD("02/30/92"); DISPLAY ID,WHEN; USE; USE EDGE. Stop the guest and extract EDGE.DBF with mcopy.
observed: Record 1 WHEN becomes the eight ASCII bytes ,)/-1124 (hex 2c292f2d31313234), rather than eight blanks. DISPLAY shows 11/24/00. The invalid bytes survive closing and reopening. This is a persistence defect beyond earlier audit L045, which described display of empty/invalid dates.
expected: A blank/invalid CTOD result must leave a valid blank date representation. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbf.md, section 5: D fields contain YYYYMMDD or blanks. This corrupts the field representation even though the table remains openable.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1654 converts every XB_D through ymd_from_jdn, including the zero/blank sentinel; only XB_U takes the blank branch at line 1675.

title: Escape and Ctrl-C cannot stop a running loop
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img, desktop route. DO LOOP. Wait 2 seconds; press Esc, wait 2 seconds; Ctrl-C, wait 2 seconds; type ? "RECOVERED" and Enter; wait 2 seconds. LOOP.PRG installs ON ESCAPE and runs DO WHILE .T. incrementing N.
observed: The screen remains at . DO LOOP; no trap output, prompt, or recovery command appears. QMP remains responsive and reports running, HLT=0. Only stopping this audit QEMU ended the session. This is failure to interrupt a program, not a claim that the infinite loop should terminate by itself.
expected: A user must be able to interrupt a mistaken loop without destroying the session. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md, ON ESCAPE/SET ESCAPE discussion. The shipped quick reference openly calls the trap inert; that documents the limitation but does not make an uncancellable loop dependable.

title: Desktop-launched status mode prints ANSI control sequences
steps: Boot flair_tenants_interactive.img with rich-fixture.img, press Ctrl+Alt+backslash, USE CLIENTS, SET STATUS ON, then ? 2+2. Allow output to settle. SET STATUS OFF restores ordinary command output.
observed: Escape sequences such as [23;1H and [0;7m fill and scroll the screen instead of positioning a status bar. The same setting works through tracer_boot.img and SAMIR.COM, so this is specific to the desktop route, not the old unrecognized SET STATUS command.
expected: SET STATUS ON should draw the status bar. Shipped quick reference qr-set.tex documents "The status bar" for STATUS; the real III+ status layout is described in dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md section 10. The DOS-route screenshot is the control.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:566 and :607 bind the status display to ANSI sequences; the DOS boot logs ANSI-WIRED/ANSI.SYS, whereas the tested desktop boot does not.

title: A successful memo replacement reads as empty until USE reopens the table
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; ? MEMO; REPLACE MEMO WITH "changed memo"; ? MEMO,LEN(MEMO); GO 2; GO 1; ? MEMO; USE; USE EDGE; ? MEMO,LEN(MEMO). Repeat with "again".
observed: Immediately after each successful REPLACE, the memo is empty and LEN is 0, even after moving away and back. Closing/reopening returns "changed memo" with length 12, then "again" on the second cycle. DBF pointers and DBT appended text are persisted correctly.
expected: Reads in the same work area should immediately reflect a successful write. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, REPLACE; dbt.md section 4 describes the memo pointer. The read-after-write requirement is also my data-consistency expectation.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:63 retains the open memo handle, while os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1763 opens a separate writable handle and appends through it; the existing reader is not refreshed.

title: An asterisk-filled numeric overflow is presented as zero
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; REPLACE SMALL WITH 99999; DISPLAY ID,SMALL. Close/reopen EDGE and display again; extract the stopped DBF.
observed: SMALL N(4,1) is stored as **** at record offset 290, but DISPLAY prints 0.0. The same false zero appears after reopening.
expected: Preserve an unmistakable overflow indication in listings instead of presenting an ordinary zero. The storage rule is in shipped Volume One u5-entries-b.tex:577: "A number too large for its field is stored as asterisks." The expectation that the listing must not conceal that failure is my usability/data-integrity judgment; I did not run a live III+ overflow listing.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:847 parses all-asterisk N fields with dec_parse and explicitly falls back to 0.0.

title: TRANSFORM reports overflow for a decimal value that fits its picture
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: ? TRANSFORM(123.4,"999.99"). Compare ? STR(123.4,6,2) and the adjacent decimal cases in transform.json.
observed: The six-character picture produces ***.** for 123.4, despite room for 123.40.
expected: The three integer and two fractional digit positions should produce 123.40. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/picture-function-templates.md section 3 and its 9,999.99 example; the arithmetic fit of this exact case is independently obvious.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/core/fn_builtins.c:1580 passes the count of digit slots to dec_format as the total width, omitting space for the decimal point.

title: INDEX ON cannot create an index for an empty table
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EMPTY; INDEX ON NAME TO ZERO; SEEK "NONE".
observed: INDEX returns 29 File is not accessible. No ZERO.NDX is created. SEEK then returns 26 Database is not indexed. EMPTY.DBF is a valid zero-record table with NAME C(12).
expected: Create a valid empty index that can receive future appends. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md, empty-root layout, and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, INDEX. This is a common new-table workflow.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1124 infers key width from the current evaluated value, which is empty when there is no record.

observed: Every abbreviation returns 16 *** Unrecognized command verb. Full spellings work for the corresponding implemented commands.
expected: Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/runtime/interpreter-and-execution-model.md:188-224 documents first-four-letter recognition. The shipped Volume One u2-commands.tex:26 explicitly instructs full spellings, so this is a historical feature gap, not an undocumented manual contradiction.

title: QUIT inside a PRG is rejected rather than exiting
steps: Run DO QUITPRG using rich-fixture.img. The file prints BEFORE QUIT, executes QUIT, and would then print AFTER QUIT.
observed: BEFORE QUIT is followed by 16 *** Unrecognized command verb and a dot prompt. The database process remains alive; AFTER QUIT is not run because the program aborted.
expected: QUIT should close files and end the database session when executed by a program. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md, QUIT; shipped Quick Reference qr-commands.tex entry QUIT says "Closes all files and leaves InitechBase".

title: Recursive internal procedures destroy the running session
steps: Fresh program-fixture.img, desktop route: DO RECINT. Wait 3 seconds, press Esc and Ctrl-C, wait 2 seconds, type ? "RECOVERED", then wait 2 seconds. RECINT.PRG calls procedure REC, whose body calls REC again.
observed: No error, return prompt or recovery output appears. This reproduced independently after a longer session and from a fresh boot. QMP still responds; the isolated capture has EIP=dbd6bba7 and ESP=00054871, outside a sensible executable/stack layout. No panic text was printed. This is an observed crash/hang; stack corruption is a diagnosis, not a proven mechanism.
expected: Bound recursive calls and report a nesting/space error without losing the session. Shipped Volume One u5-entries-a.tex:336-341 says procedures may call themselves "to a depth of 64". Safe handling beyond the supported depth is also my reliability requirement.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/proc.c:592-607 allocates an 8192-byte automatic body per call; recursive stack growth may overwrite guest state before the intended nesting limit.

title: PACK with two open indexes leaves live index state unusable
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE CLIENTS; INDEX ON NAME TO BYNAME; INDEX ON BAL TO BYBAL; SET INDEX TO BYNAME,BYBAL; SET ORDER TO 1; PACK; REINDEX; GO TOP; LIST. Then CLOSE INDEX; GO TOP; LIST. Finally USE; USE CLIENTS INDEX BYNAME,BYBAL; GO TOP; LIST.
observed: PACK reports success, but REINDEX returns 114 Index damaged, GO TOP returns 5 Record is out of range, and LIST returns 10 Syntax error. Closing indexes restores physical traversal; reopening both restores sorted traversal. The one-index control passes. This reproduced without any deleted records, so record compaction is not required. The stopped DBF and NDX bytes remain readable; persistent index corruption is not claimed.
expected: PACK must preserve usable open indexes, rebuilding them as needed. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md section 10 (PACK).
source_guess: Guess: inspect the multi-index lifetime across os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:945-959 and fs/ndx.c:2655 (ndx_rebuild). A single-index run does not reproduce it.

title: INDEX ON fails when the current pointer is at EOF
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE CLIENTS; GO BOTTOM; SKIP; ? EOF(),RECNO(); INDEX ON NAME TO EOFIDX. Then GO TOP; INDEX ON NAME TO TOPIDX.
observed: EOF is true at record 4. The first INDEX returns 29 File is not accessible and creates no file; the same expression succeeds after GO TOP.
expected: INDEX ON scans the table independently of the incoming current-record position. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, INDEX; my equivalent-input expectation is that moving to EOF does not make the output file inaccessible.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1124-1130 derives key width/type from the current record before scanning. At EOF a character field evaluates as a zero-length value.

title: A valid blank date prevents creation of a date index
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; INDEX ON WHEN TO BLANKDAT. EDGE record 3 has eight blank bytes in WHEN. Control on another fresh copy: REPLACE ALL WHEN WITH CTOD("01/01/92"); GO TOP; INDEX ON WHEN TO VALIDATE.
observed: The original table returns 9 Data type mismatch. Filling all dates with valid dates and moving to GO TOP succeeds. The shipped STAFF/HIRED date-index example also succeeds. This is specifically the valid blank date case, not missing date indexing generally.
expected: Blank dates are legal database values and must be indexable alongside ordinary dates. Named references: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbf.md section 5 (blank D fields) and ndx.md section 4.2 (date keys).
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:244-249 accepts XB_N and XB_D, but not the XB_U representation returned for a blank DBF date.

title: INDEX accepts 101-character keys beyond the III+ maximum
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; GO TOP; INDEX ON LEFT(WIDE,100) TO KEY100; GO TOP; INDEX ON LEFT(WIDE,101) TO KEY101. Extract both NDX files after stopping.
observed: Both succeed. KEY101.NDX records key_length=101 in the little-endian word at offset 12. A direct 254-character key is rejected with 29 File is not accessible, rather than the specific key-size diagnostic.
expected: Reject keys longer than 100 with the III+ index-too-big diagnostic. Named reference: the III+ message catalog "Index is too big (100 char maximum)" and dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, INDEX limits. This is a compatibility/boundary defect; I did not feed the generated 101-byte index into a live III+ interpreter.

title: A corrupt existing NDX is reported as nonexistent

observed: The command says 1 File does not exist, although the file is present and extractable from the same image.
expected: Distinguish a malformed index from a missing pathname, so the user can take the right repair action. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md, header validation invariants; the accurate-diagnostic requirement is my usability judgment.

title: The ordinary dot prompt truncates commands at 128 bytes
steps: Use desktop route with default SET STATUS OFF. Type the exact 254-character command in keys.json: ? LEN(" followed by 245 x characters, then "). Press Enter. Repeat the 255-character variant with 246 y characters.
observed: Only the first 128 bytes are accepted; the remaining 126/127 keystrokes ring the bell. The closing quote/parenthesis is lost and execution reports 35 Unterminated string. This is not a legitimate rejection of a 255-byte command: the documented 254-byte case fails too.
expected: Accept the promised 254-character line. Shipped Volume One ua-keys.tex:20-22 says printable characters are taken "up to 254 characters"; u2-commands.tex:16 repeats the limit. Reject an overlong line coherently rather than executing its truncated prefix.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:650-654 uses the cooked DOS stream when status is off; the observed 128-byte cap occurs below SAMIR line framing.

title: A 7018-byte, 1000-line program fails with insufficient memory
steps: Fresh program-fixture.img: DO SHORT1K. The fixture sets N=0, repeats N=N+1 1000 times, prints N and returns; its exact CRLF file size is 7018 bytes.
observed: 43 Insufficient memory is returned without running the program. An ordinary compact program with IF, CASE, LOOP, EXIT and procedures runs successfully in the control session.
expected: This small program should fit the advertised file limit and a 16 MiB workstation. Shipped Volume One u5-entries-a.tex:331-333 states a maximum of 8191 characters. The 1000-line case is explicitly requested by this audit brief. This is a capacity limitation, not a crash.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:54 fixes FLOW_MAX_LINES at 512, an additional limit not stated with the documented file-size limit.

title: DO inside a PRG cannot call another existing PRG file
steps: Fresh control-fixture.img: DO OUTER. OUTER.PRG contains DO USEPRG, then prints CHILD RETURNED. USEPRG.PRG exists and works when invoked directly at the dot prompt.
observed: The nested call returns 16 *** Unrecognized command verb. CHILD RETURNED is never printed. Internal named procedures work in FLOW.PRG.
expected: Resolve a DO target to either a procedure or another program file. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md:71-85, resolution order. The shipped manual describes only internal procedure calls from a program, so this is a historical capability gap.

title: RETRY in an error handler does not retry the failed statement
steps: Fresh control-fixture.img: DO RETRY. Main code prints XX before it exists. Its ON ERROR procedure assigns XX=7, increments TRYCNT, and executes RETRY. Main code then prints DONE,TRYCNT.
observed: Only DONE 1 appears; the repaired ? XX is never retried, so 7 is missing. The program returns normally. A bare dot-prompt RETRY is also unrecognized, but the finding rests on the valid handler context.
expected: RETRY must execute the failing command again after the handler fixes its cause. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md:232-243 quotes the III+ HELP behavior and the ERRORPRG.PRG usage.

title: BOF stays false for a physically empty database

observed: The count is 0 and EOF is true, but BOF is false both immediately after USE and after GO TOP.
expected: For an empty file, both boundary predicates should be true. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/navigation-query-display.md:999. That local specification includes cross-implementation corroboration; I did not mint this case in a live III+ session.
